question.text: Which of the following disqualifies an entity from acting as the independent valuer for Lotus Capital AIF (a Cat II fund)?

answer.text: The valuer has 5 years of experience in unlisted securities valuation
The valuer is an IBBI-registered valuer with an ICAI member as the authorised person
The valuer is a wholly-owned subsidiary of the AIF's sponsor
The valuer is a holding company of a SEBI-registered credit rating agency

explanation.text: The Logic: Per PDF Section 11.12, the independent valuer 'shall NOT be an associate of manager or sponsor or trustee of the AIF.' A sponsor subsidiary is an associate and automatically disqualified. The 5-yr experience exceeds the 3-yr minimum; IBBI+ICAI combo is the gold standard; and holding company of a SEBI-registered CRA is explicitly one of the permitted eligibility routes. The Trap: The other three options describe ELIGIBLE valuers. The INDEPENDENCE test (no associate relationship with M/S/T) is the gating criterion — qualifications alone are insufficient if there's any sponsor/manager relationship. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C tests the same independence rule. The 'associate' definition under AIF Regulations mirrors the Companies Act 2013 Sec 2(6) 'related party' concept. XXI-B (PM) has similar custodian/valuer segregation rules for PMS. Manager's Pro-Tip: Document the independence check in your valuer-appointment file: shareholder chain, board overlap, past commercial relationships. SEBI inspectors routinely ask for this independence declaration during Cat I/II inspections.
